Byomkesh Bakshi.description: The protagonist and sharp detective known as a 'truth-seeker' who investigates complex cases with keen observation.

Ajit Bandyopadhyay.description: The narrator and close companion of Byomkesh, who documents their adventures and assists in investigations.

Doctor Suresh Rakshit.description: A family physician and tenant of Bishu Pal, involved in the central plot and later revealed as an accomplice.

Bishu Pal.description: A wealthy moneylender who fakes paralysis to plot a murder, central to the story's mystery.

Abhay Ghosal.description: A notorious debtor of Bishu Pal, accused of multiple crimes and ultimately the murder victim.

Rama Pati babu.description: A diligent and hardworking police officer investigating Abhay Ghosal’s murder.

Sushil babu.description: The police surgeon responsible for examining Bishu Pal to verify his claims of paralysis.

Dr. Asim Sen.description: A senior doctor and acquaintance of Byomkesh, consulted for medical expertise regarding paralysis.

Dustu Chakra.description: Bengali for 'Wicked Plan', the title of the chapter.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, the city where the story is set.

Amherst Street.description: A well-known street in Calcutta, serving as a key location in the narrative.

Marwaris.description: An Indian ethnic group traditionally known for their business acumen, referenced in the context of moneylending.

Gurkha.description: A member of a Nepalese ethnic group, often employed as security guards in India for their reputation of bravery.

reserve bank.description: Refers to the Reserve Bank of India, the country's central banking institution.

gaddi.description: A low mattress or seat used by traders or moneylenders in their offices, especially among Marwaris.

compounder.description: A medical assistant who prepares and dispenses medicines in a doctor's dispensary.

dewan.description: A long, backless couch or mattress commonly used for lounging in Indian homes.
